title: Experimental hosting blend proposal - quick notes
body:
Goal:
- Sketch a pragmatic POC approach that blends hosted, dedicated and private lanes to hit three customer constraints: 1) sub-150ms median tail for interactive queries, 2) predictable monthly spend for peak campaign windows, 3) hard data isolation for regulated flows.

High-level idea ("hosting blend"):
- Traffic categories: interactive UI queries (low token, latency-sensitive), batch/rerank jobs (higher token counts, throughput priority), and regulated transactions (sensitive PHI/PII).
- Map categories to runtime lanes: hosted fast-path for interactive, dedicated reserved pool for throughput and predictable QoS, private deployment for regulated transactions with local KMS and audit logs.
- Smart router (policy engine) performs per-request decisions: tags on request (sensitivity, user tier, max-latency), historical latency shaping, and cost-aware fallback.

Architecture notes:
- Edge ingress -> auth + tagger -> policy router -> lane selector.
- Hosted lane: latest curated open model (opt-quant), autoscaling ephemeral pods, streaming responses enabled. Use prefix cache for top-k prompts.
- Dedicated lane: pinned model versions and GPU sizing for 8–16k token windows, reserved capacity with burst allowance; set queue depth controls for backpressure.
- Private lane: on-customer VPC connector with TLS mutual auth, offline model artifact sync (signed), HSM-backed keys.
- KV shard idea: keep small session KV cached at router for hosted fast-path; for dedicated/private use distributed KV with affinity to GPU hosts to reduce KV hop.

Fallback and graceful degradation:
- Primary plan: if dedicated lane at capacity, router can route to hosted (if allowed by data policy) or enqueue with SLA promise.
- For regulated flows, if private is unavailable, fail closed (reject) or return soft-denied template depending on customer preference.
- Circuit-breaker thresholds: 90% GPU util -> shift non-critical traffic to hosted; 98% -> shed lowest-priority routes.

POC acceptance criteria (suggested):
- Latency: 99th <= 250ms for interactive test set (avg prompt 60 tokens) when routing to hosted/dedicated hybrid.
- Throughput: dedicated lane sustains 300 concurrent requests with 1.5k token avg with <10% tail latency increase on mixed workload.
- Isolation: regulated traffic always shows private-host headers, end-to-end audit trace present in logs.
- Cost: blended unit cost for mixed traffic <= customer target (example: $0.0009 per generated token equivalent for the test mix).

Sample test matrix for POC (to implement in first 2 weeks):
- Scenario A: interactive chat, 50 RPS, avg 60 tokens, 95% should hit hosted fast-path.
- Scenario B: heavy assistant task, 8 RPS, avg 1.2k tokens, should hit dedicated lane.
- Scenario C: regulated ingestion, 5 RPS, PII present, must hit private lane with KMS encryption.
- Run mixture traffic test to validate routing decisions and observe fallback behavior under controlled capacity reductions.

Instrumentation and dashboards:
- Per-route breakdown (tokens, requests, median/95/99 latencies), lane-level GPU utilization, queue depths, and prefix cache hit ratio.
- Business signals: cost per 1k tokens, errors by data sensitivity tag.
- Add alerting for policy-router anomalies (e.g., >5% misroutes).

Operational runbook (brief):
- Canary rollout: 5% traffic to dedicated lane for 24h, monitor latencies and cost delta, then 25% for 48h, full after sweep.
- Failure modes: GPU OOM -> automatically restart job on dedicated lane with reduced batch size; if repeated, route new requests to hosted.
- Emergency rollback: global toggle to force all non-regulated traffic to hosted.

Rough cost/size estimate for POC cluster (customer-supplied numbers approximate):
- Dedicated pool: 4 x A40-equivalent GPUs, reserved for 2 weeks of testing.
- Hosted estimate: ephemeral usage spike 1000 vCPU-seconds on average, incremental token spend.
- Private: single-node (for POC) with minimal SLOs but full auditing enabled.

Open questions / known risks:
- Data residency: how many users will require strict private-only routing? Need customer input to size private node.
- KV consistency across lanes: strong consistency will increase latency for shared-session use-cases. Consider session-affinity to a lane.
- Cost modeling: can we provide a simple calculator for customers to see blended cost across different mixes? (action: SE to prototype).
- Model parity: minor generation differences across quant and non-quant kernels may impact customer QA; need an eval set.

Next steps (owner tags):
- Sofia: draft quick confluence explainer + high-level slide for customer meeting (2 days).
- Marco: run 1-hour synthetic run to measure hosted fast-path cache hit impact (3 days).
- Priya: scope private node sizing questions and KMS checklist to send to customer (tomorrow).
- Ethan: sketch policy-router config primitives and sample rules for canary/fallback (2 days).

Meeting prep checklist for kickoff:
- Customer constraints: list of regulated flows and must-not-leave-region flags.
- Expected traffic shape (RPS, token length distribution).
- Cost targets and preferred fallbacks.
- Decision on failure semantics for private flows (reject vs degrade).

Notes to self / scribbles:
- Consider a "transient compute lane" concept: ephemeral high-priority pods that borrow dedicated GPUs for short windows to reduce queuing without increasing long-term reservations.
- Keep an eye on quant mismatch: create small eval harness that runs same prompts across hosted/dedicated/private builds and diffs outputs.
- If customer wants deterministic output, we need to pin model + seed and document any kernel-induced variance.

References / links to internal artifacts (for followup):
- SE hosting patterns (confluence) — compare with requested POC scope.
- infra playbook ticket JIRA-SE-5123 (linked above).

End summary:
- This POC should demonstrate a lightweight but practical hybrid hosting approach that proves routing policies, fallbacks, and cost visibility. Keep the first experiment narrow (3 scenarios), instrument aggressively, and iterate on policy knobs rather than trying to perfect model parity in week 0.

Unresolved: customer-provided constraints and final cost target.
